name: FLORES-101
description: The FLORES-101 evaluation benchmark consists of 3001 sentences extracted from English Wikipedia and translated into 101 languages by professional translators, enabling better assessment of model quality on low-resource languages.
creator: Naman Goyal, Cynthia Gao, Vishrav Chaudhary, Peng-Jen Chen, Guillaume Wenzek, Da Ju, Sanjana Krishnan, Marc’Aurelio Ranzato, Francisco Guzmán, Angela Fan (Facebook AI Research)
citeAs: Goyal et al. (2021). The FLORES-101 Evaluation Benchmark for Low-Resource and Multilingual Machine Translation.
rai:dataCollection: Sentences were sourced from English Wikipedia, Wikinews, Wikijunior, and WikiVoyage, ensuring a broad range of topics.
rai:dataCollectionRawData: Sentences extracted from English Wikipedia and other Wikimedia sources.
rai:dataAnnotationProtocol: Translations were performed by professional translators, with multiple rounds of quality checks and evaluations to ensure high translation quality.
rai:annotatorDemographics: Translators from diverse regions including East Asia, South Asia, Southern Europe, Latin America, and North America.
rai:dataSocialImpact: The dataset aims to improve machine translation for low-resource languages, fostering inclusivity in technology.
rai:dataBiases: The authors note that the dataset may not fully represent all low-resource languages and could be biased towards languages with more available resources.
rai:dataLimitations: The dataset may not cover all linguistic features of low-resource languages and is limited to the quality of translations provided by professional translators.
